subject: journey/nautilus
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. A single landscape 3:2 illustration for the historical atlas sketchbook of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. A nineteenth-century naturalist's field sketch in graphite and sepia pen with restrained transparent watercolour washes on warm ivory paper. Fine irregular parallel hatching, economical contour lines, a few details sharply observed; leave areas of cream paper around irregular unfinished edges. One coherent scene that reads at small sizes. No captions, labels, border, binding, signatures, photorealism, modern equipment, or Disney submarine designs. View from the dark saloon through a broad oval observation window. A huge solitary eye with a restrained sea-green iris and the curled sucker-lined arm of a reddish cephalopod pass just outside, its mantle fading into green water. Naturalist pencil detail on suckers; keep creature anatomy coherent.
